# Design Standards

## Layout Consistency
- Use a consistent grid or flex layout system across all views.
- Align elements to a clear baseline and maintain predictable spacing.
- Avoid arbitrary positioning; follow established layout patterns.

## Spacing System
- Define a fixed spacing scale (e.g., 4px multiples).
- Apply spacing consistently for margins, padding, and gaps.
- Do not mix arbitrary values; adhere to the scale for uniformity.

## Typography Hierarchy
- Establish clear levels: headings, subheadings, body, captions.
- Use consistent font sizes, weights, and line heights.
- Limit font families to one primary and one secondary (if needed).

## Color Usage
- Define a primary, secondary, and neutral palette.
- Use colors consistently for actions, states, and emphasis.
- Ensure sufficient contrast for text and interactive elements.
- Reserve accent colors for highlights, not structural elements.

## Accessibility
- Meet WCAG AA standards for contrast and readability.
- Provide visible focus states for all interactive elements.
- Use semantic HTML elements to support screen readers.
- Avoid relying solely on color to convey meaning.

## Component Consistency
- Reuse components instead of duplicating styles.
- Keep components small, focused, and predictable.
- Ensure consistent behavior across similar components (e.g., buttons, inputs).
- Document reusable patterns in a shared design system.

## Clarity & Usability
- Prioritize simplicity; avoid visual clutter.
- Ensure actions are discoverable and feedback is immediate.
- Favor intuitive defaults and minimize user effort.
- Test designs for readability and ease of interaction.
